tonight.headline: 0-2, last in points scored, and the fix is a trade rather than a claim
body: You have scored 183.26 points, the fewest of any team in this league, and you are 0-2. JuiceJam project 123.05 to your 118.87, a 48% win probability. They start Jahmyr Gibbs and Kenneth Walker at running back and that is most of the gap.

There is nothing on this wire worth your waiver priority. Priority here never resets, so a claim costs you 3rd place in the order for the remaining fifteen weeks, and the best thing available is a defence worth about a point. Both real upgrades today are trades, and trades cost nothing.

case.label: The asymmetry, since it drives every no below
case.body: Chem resets weekly, so this morning's Chem brief files two claims. Here, ESPN never reorders: use the claim and you sit 10th until January. The bar is therefore a starter-level need, and you do not have one — your weakest starting slot is tight end and the answer to it is already on your bench.

case.label: Where the points actually are
case.body: Your current lineup projects 118.80 and ESPN's own best arrangement of the same fourteen players is 119.00 — two tenths apart, and that gap is the flex, not the tight end. Worth saying plainly: the swap in the first card makes your ESPN projection 0.7 WORSE, because ESPN still prices Loveland at 9.9. I am telling you to make it anyway, against the number, on a player who has caught one pass for three yards. The real gains are the two trades — 2.5 and 3.7 a week, 37.9 and 45.7 across the season, both positive for the other side on both pricings.

case.label: The opponent's one hole
case.body: JuiceJam's flex is Chris Godwin at 8.8 and Nico Collins is out on their bench. Everything else they start is healthy. This is not a matchup you win with a wire pickup; it is one you win if Barkley plays and Taylor scores again.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Barkley being ruled out. He is your RB2 and Philadelphia do not play until Monday night, so you will know long before you have to decide — but if he sits, your flex and bench cannot cover it and this becomes a very different week.

doFirst.title: Start T.J. Hockenson over Colston Loveland
doFirst.subtitle: Loveland has one catch for three yards all season. This is the second day this card has been written and it has not been made.

case.label: Where ESPN and the reporting flatly disagree
case.body: ESPN projects Loveland 9.9 and Hockenson 9.2 and has your lineup the wrong way round on that basis. Loveland's actual production across two games is ONE reception for THREE yards. Yahoo's Monday piece on the Bears is titled around the idea that Tyson Bagent 'must unleash' him — that is an argument about what Chicago should do, not a description of what they have done. Believe the reporting.

case.label: Who is throwing, for both of them
case.body: Loveland catches from Tyson Bagent: Caleb Williams pulled his hamstring on a non-contact play in the fourth quarter of Week 2 and Ben Johnson called him week-to-week. Chicago are implied at 20.0 against a Philadelphia defence Yahoo describes as 'stout against the running game' too, so there is no script that helps. Hockenson catches from Kyler Murray, confirmed by the team Monday as cleared from concussion protocol and starting.

case.label: Hockenson's role, stated without overselling it
case.body: 69.2% snap share in Week 2 and 19 routes on Carson Wentz's 24 dropbacks, with Josh Oliver running four. He is unambiguously the receiving tight end. But he has 9 targets in two games and Murray has thrown five passes all season, so the Murray upgrade is an inference, not evidence — DK Network's piece on Murray's return names Justin Jefferson as the main beneficiary and gives no tight end usage at all. This is a low-end TE1, not a fix.

case.label: Why it is still easily the right move
case.body: You are choosing between a secure role with thin volume and a role that has produced one catch in two weeks behind an undrafted backup. It costs nothing, spends no priority, and reverses next Tuesday. If the Kittle trade below lands, this card disappears entirely.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Chicago target Loveland six or more times against Philadelphia while Hockenson stays under four in a low-dropback Vikings game. That would say the Bagent-unleashes-Loveland thesis was right and the tight end seat goes back. Minnesota won 9-3 in Week 2 on 24 dropbacks, so the low-volume version of Hockenson is a real risk.

case.label: Why I am not upgrading the odds, and where I did

I am going back to LIKELY, and the only honest reason to do so is new information: yesterday both quarterbacks were injury flags, today both are confirmed absences with named-coach quotes and no timeline. If that were not true I would have left it alone, because flip-flopping on unchanged evidence is how this brief stops being worth reading.

case.body: You already own Matthew Golden. Watson and Golden are the same two-man receiver room on a Green Bay offence that ran 50 plays in Week 2, and Golden leads in snaps and routes while Watson leads in targets and touchdowns. Acquiring Watson concentrates two of your starting slots into one offence. If that bothers you, ask for George Kittle instead — he prices at +2.8 for you and +13.8 for them, he is on their bench behind Isaiah Likely, and he solves your tight end slot permanently rather than for a week.

whatWentWrong.title: I told you yesterday to claim the Giants D/ST here. In this league that would have been a real mistake.
whatWentWrong.lead: It would have cost you 3rd waiver priority for the rest of the season, permanently, for a defence. And the defence itself is now wrong.

case.label: The rule the card broke
case.body: This brief's own standing finding, recorded correct on 16 September and every run since, is: never spend IPADE waiver priority on a defence. Yesterday's card did exactly that. Priority here never resets — one claim and you sit 10th of 10 until January.

case.label: And the pick was wrong on its own terms
case.body: The Draft Sharks ranking that put New York 2nd predates Jaxson Dart's sprained MCL. Dart is out two to four weeks per SNY, Jameis Winston starts, and the Giants line moved from -5.5 to -3 with a 40.5 total. So the card would have burned a season-long asset on a defence whose own offence had just lost its quarterback.

case.label: What it actually cost
case.body: Nothing, because you did not make the move — the Ravens D/ST is still in your lineup and your priority is still 3. This is the one place this week where not acting on the brief was better than acting on it, and it should be said plainly.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing about defences. The rule stands and I am restating it: in IPADE, the priority is spent on a starting running back or receiver or it is not spent at all.

By my math it's worth about +13 to you this week and about +2.5 to me, so you're getting the better end of it in the short term and I'm fine with that because I need a receiver more than a backup QB. case.label: The structural argument
case.body: Team 13 start Josh Allen at 22.8. Lamar Jackson sits on their bench at 20.1 and scores them literally nothing every week, because a league with one quarterback slot cannot use two. case.body: You are asking for a top-three quarterback by name and offering a second-year running back. The computation says both sides gain on both pricings — +3.7 and +45.7 for you, +1.6 and +21.9 for them — but managers do not trade Lamar Jackson for Bhayshul Tuten because a solver told them to. Send it, expect a no, and expect a counter asking for Jonathan Taylor, which is the answer no.

He has 559 passing yards, 6th in the NFL, with 2 passing touchdowns and a rushing score, and Week 2 was quiet mainly because Zay Flowers missed it with a hamstring. doNotChase.name: Jaguars D/ST
doNotChase.lead: The best defence you could claim, worth about a point over the Ravens, and it would cost you third waiver priority until January.

case.label: The honest arithmetic
case.body: Jaguars 7.1 against the Ravens' 6.0. That is 1.1 points, in a week where Baltimore are in the highest-total game on the board at 52.5 and Jacksonville are -2.5 against a New England side implied at 21.5. The Jacksonville side of it is genuinely better.

case.label: Why it still loses, and why this is the standing rule
case.body: IPADE waiver order never resets. Filing this claim moves you from 3rd to 10th for the remaining fifteen weeks. You are 0-2 and last in points scored, which means the probability you need that priority for a genuine starter — a running back going down, a breakout receiver — is high. Trading 3rd priority for a point at defence is the worst price on the board.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing at defence. This rule has now been recorded correct on six separate runs and yesterday's brief broke it with the Giants card. The bar is a starting running back or receiver.

doNotChase.name: James Cook III
doNotChase.ownership: trade target, not a wire player
doNotChase.lead: The trade that this week's numbers say is mutual and next week's say is theft. Do not send it.

case.label: What the weekly solver reports
case.body: Hockenson for James Cook: +5.4 for you, +5.7 for Metcalf Gala. It passes the runbook's both-sides-gain test on weekly pricing and would have been publishable as a proposal.

case.label: What the season numbers report
case.body: Minus 79.8 for them. Cook's season projection is 253.2; the Aaron Jones who would replace him is 173.4. The weekly gain exists only because Dallas Goedert is doubtful and projects 0.0, so any tight end fills a hole worth 9-ish points this week and nothing after it.

case.label: Why it is in the brief
case.body: Because it is the clearest example this week of the runbook's own stated limitation — that trades priced on one week are the wrong unit — and of why that limitation is now fixable. Every proposal above was computed both ways and published only where both agree.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing. If Metcalf Gala offered it to you, take it.

doNotChase.sources: ESPN league file · optimal-lineup solver, weekly and season

doNotChase.name: Khalil Shakir
doNotChase.lead: Carried as a watch row here and in Chem for five runs. Closing it in both leagues on the same number.

case.label: The usage that ends it
case.body: Week 2 at Detroit: 50.4% snap share, 60% route share, 21.4% target share, 36 of 74 offensive snaps. Keon Coleman led Buffalo's receivers at 55 snaps, and SI's snap-count piece notes three tight ends played more than Buffalo's second-most-used receiver.

case.label: Why the old test kept passing
case.body: The clause was target-count based: six or more against Detroit makes him a claim. He drew six and the clause fired. Six targets on a 60% route share is a worse fact than six targets on its own, and the clause never asked about routes.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A 75%+ route share, not a target count.

doNotChase.sources: RotoWire box-score breakdown · SI · ESPN league file

doNotChase.name: Jake Ferguson
doNotChase.lead: Carried forward unchanged for a third run. His clause fired again and the answer is still no, for a new reason.

case.label: The case for him
case.body: 8.7 this week against Loveland's 9.9 and Hockenson's 9.2, in the 52.5-point Brazil game — the highest total on the board. On environment alone he is the best tight end spot available to you.

case.label: Why it is still no
case.body: He is a waiver claim and Hockenson is already on your bench. You do not need to spend 3rd-priority-until-January to fix a tight end slot you can fix for free with the first card. And if the Sack Steel Boys trade lands as Kittle instead of Watson, the position is solved outright.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Hockenson getting hurt while you still hold priority. Nothing short of that.

settled.title: Claim the Giants D/ST here, dropping the Ravens (21 September)
settled.result: Withdrawn, and it should never have been written. It broke this brief's own standing rule against spending never-resetting priority on a defence, and the Draft Sharks ranking behind it predates Jaxson Dart's sprained MCL. You did not make the move, which is the only reason it cost nothing.

settled.title: Start Colston Loveland at tight end (16, 20 and 21 September, five runs)
settled.result: One catch for three yards across two games, and he is still in your starting slot. Yesterday's brief finally called for the bench and the lineup was not changed. Re-issued as the first card with the Bagent evidence attached.

settled.title: Downgrade the Stafford-for-Watson offer from LIKELY to EVEN (21 September, evening)
settled.result: Reversed back to LIKELY, and only on new evidence: both Sack Steel Boys quarterbacks are now confirmed out by named-coach reporting rather than carrying injury flags, and their starting quarterback slot projects 0.0. Their computed gain rose from single digits to +13.5.

settled.title: Report season-long value as unavailable, per the runbook's limitations (standing)
settled.result: The runbook is out of date — seasonProj is published on every roster and wire entry. All three trades above are priced weekly AND season, and the Hockenson-for-Cook proposal is rejected purely because the two disagree by 80 points.

settled.title: Never spend IPADE waiver priority on a defence (16 September, every run)
settled.result: Held for a sixth run, and it is what makes yesterday's Giants card wrong. The best available defence gains 1.1 points and costs 3rd priority until January.

settled.title: Keep Matthew Golden in the flex over Devaughn Vele (21 September)
settled.result: Held. The two project within two tenths, and Jayden Reed being ruled out with a neck/back injury concentrates Green Bay's target tree onto Golden and Watson. Vele's Las Vegas draw is the harder one.

settled.title: Hold MarShawn Lloyd rather than drop him (21 September)
settled.result: Held, on one fact: Josh Jacobs is on the Commissioner's Exempt List. I still could not find 2026 snap-count reporting on Lloyd himself, so his tile stays dashed.

settled.title: Hold Jason Myers at kicker (18 September, six runs)
settled.result: Seattle are -6.5 and implied 23.5 against a Mariota-led Washington. Nothing on waivers justifies a season-long priority. The seat has been right every run.

settled.title: Re-verify both standing trades structurally rather than carrying them forward (21 September)
settled.result: Done again today from scratch on the 12:52 file. Stafford-for-Watson and Tuten-for-Lamar both still compute positive for both sides on both pricings; Garrett Wilson-for-Allen survives but at +0.4 for them, which is why it is ranked last and flagged as noise.

settled.title: Check the other team's slot column before naming anyone in a trade (standing rule)
settled.result: Checked on all three. Watson and Lamar Jackson are both slot 20, their benches. Josh Allen is slot 0, a starter, which is exactly why that offer is graded LONGSHOT and ranked third.

settled.title: Read settings.scoring and the flex slot live every run (Step 2, standing)
settled.result: IPADE is 1.0 per reception and the flex is slot 23, RB/WR/TE — both unchanged. It matters this week: the TE-eligible flex is why Hockenson and Loveland compete with your receivers and why the Kittle alternative is worth naming.

settled.title: Cross-check every source against its date (20 September, standing rule)
settled.result: It earned its keep. Research on this run discarded 2025-dated pages on Purdy's toe, Warren-versus-Gainwell, Achane's Week 1, Monangai's rookie year and a 2022 Packers snap count — and caught three roster premises that were simply false for 2026: Kenneth Gainwell is a Buccaneer, Travis Etienne is a Saint, and Isaiah Likely is a Giant.

cannotSee.label: Saquon Barkley's MRI result
cannotSee.body: He had a precautionary MRI on Monday for the stinger. No result was public as of 13:00 UTC Tuesday. Sirianni's position via Rapoport is that it is minor and he plays through it, but that is a coach on Monday, not a scan. Philadelphia play Monday night, so the real answer arrives on Wednesday's practice report and again on Friday — both after this brief.

cannotSee.label: No Week 3 injury report exists yet for anyone
cannotSee.body: Clubs file their first Week 3 practice reports on Wednesday 23 September. Every injury judgement here rests on Monday and Tuesday beat reporting. Only Green Bay and Atlanta have filed estimated reports, because they play Thursday.

cannotSee.label: Whether Kyler Murray actually changes anything for Hockenson
cannotSee.body: He is confirmed cleared and starting, but he has thrown five passes all season and the only Murray-to-Hockenson evidence I found is an August training-camp note about a red-zone connection. DK Network's piece on his return names Justin Jefferson as the beneficiary and gives no tight end usage at all. The first card rests mainly on Loveland being bad, not on Hockenson being good.

cannotSee.label: Rivals' pending claims
cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own. Sack Steel Boys hold priority 7 and need a quarterback; Bo Nix, Tyler Shough, Kyler Murray, Jordan Love, Bryce Young, C.J. Stroud and Sam Darnold all clear at 01:00. If one of them lands there, the first trade is dead and I cannot see it coming.

cannotSee.label: Week 2's fantasy scores are gone from the file
cannotSee.body: The snapshot has rolled to scoringPeriod 3 and every 'actual' is null. Your 183.26 points-for is the only surviving aggregate; every box-score line in this brief comes from beat reporting rather than from ESPN.

cannotSee.label: Devaughn Vele's and Rashee Rice's snap and target shares
cannotSee.body: No 2026-dated source published a snap-share or target-share percentage for Vele, and the 26.2% target share widely quoted for Rice is a 2025 figure from a preseason preview. Rice's 12.8% is a single-game count from Week 2, not a season rate. Both rows are written on raw targets rather than shares, and I would rather say that than quote a rate I cannot source.

cannotSee.label: MarShawn Lloyd's actual role
cannotSee.body: Dashed tile. No 2026 snap-count or carry-share reporting on him at all. He is held on the Josh Jacobs exempt-list fact alone, which is a fact about someone else.

cannotSee.label: Defence grades are judgement, not data, before Week 4
cannotSee.body: Every matchup read in this brief comes from the Week 3 spread and over/under — implied team totals — not from a defensive sample. Two games is not a sample. Where I had no odds and no reporting, the tile is dashed rather than graded average.

cannotSee.label: Whether the three-way Team 13 situation can be worked at all
cannotSee.body: Two of the three trades above go to the same manager and they are mutually exclusive in practice. I cannot see his preferences, his message history, or whether he has already traded with someone else this week. Pick one.

cannotSee.label: This brief does not refresh itself
cannotSee.body: Written at 13:10 UTC Tuesday. Waivers process in about twelve hours, Green Bay and Atlanta play in roughly two days, and the next brief lands after the first of those. Anything that moves in between is invisible here.
